sections.content: How many people are "typists and related keyboard occupations"?

5,375 people

were counted on the census as "typists and related keyboard occupations" in England and Wales in March 2021.

This makes this type of work the tenth least common occupation reported on the census.

People working as typists and in related keyboard occupations type letters, memos, reports and other documents from draft, handwritten or dictated matter, using appropriate software packages.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "typists and related keyboard occupations" there were more women than men (89.2% compared with 10.8%).

This means "typists and related keyboard occupations" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "secretarial and related occupations".

Men made up 10.8% and women made up 89.2% of "typists and related keyboard occupations"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "typists and related keyboard occupations" included:

  • housekeepers and related occupations
  • higher level teaching assistants
  • educational support assistants

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "typists and related keyboard occupations" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 65 years or older. Of the whole working population 4.2% were aged 65 years or older. For people working as "typists and related keyboard occupations", 16.7% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "typists and related keyboard occupations" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "typists and related keyboard occupations" included:

  • undertakers, mortuary and crematorium assistants
  • caretakers
  • hospital porters

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "typists and related keyboard occupations" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "typists and related keyboard occupations" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "typists and related keyboard occupations", 18.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (57% compared with 43%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (67.2%) than self-employed (32.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Sheffield, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
